title: A Celebrations Table
strapline: Every family celebrates — bring yours to the table and share it with us.
intent: A shared celebrations table invites families to bring their own festivals and special days, so every child sees their culture valued.
Exploring how different families celebrate builds real knowledge of the world and a warm respect for difference.
Handling artefacts, foods and decorations from many celebrations sparks curiosity, questions and vocabulary.
Talking about their own family's special days grows a strong sense of self, belonging and pride.
The theme runs all year, welcoming whatever celebrations matter to the children right now.
implementation: Keep a special table or shelf where celebration objects, photos and stories from families can be displayed and explored with care.
Invite families to share a celebration that matters to them — a festival, a wedding, a naming, a new year — with an object, photo or food.
Wonder together respectfully: 'This is special to Zainab's family — I wonder what happens on this day.'
Feed in knowledge lightly and warmly — what's celebrated, how, and what the objects mean — never treating any as strange.
Let children whose celebration it is take the lead, telling the room about their special day.
Follow the children's questions and keep the table changing with the calendar and the families.
key_questions: What special days does your family celebrate?
What happens on this day — what do people do?
What is this object for, and why is it special?
How is this celebration the same as yours — how is it different?
How does it feel to celebrate with your family?

impact.text: Children talk about their own family's celebrations and notice other families celebrate differently.
Children show respect and curiosity for festivals and traditions unlike their own.
Children explore celebration artefacts and ask real questions about them.
Children whose celebration it is share it with pride and confidence.
Children build vocabulary about celebrations, foods and traditions.

enhancements: A dedicated celebrations table or shelf that changes through the year with families' input.
A family invitation to share a festival, object, photo or food.
A 'special days' book collecting each family's celebration in words and pictures.
Artefacts and decorations from a range of celebrations to handle carefully.
Story books about festivals and special days from around the world.

playing_exploring: Children explore celebration objects and photos with genuine curiosity.
They handle and ask about things from festivals across the world.
active_learning: Children whose celebration it is take pride in sharing it fully.
They stay engaged with the changing table across the year.
creating_thinking: Children compare celebrations, noticing what's the same and different.
They connect the table to their own family's special days.
